answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake before it may send offers, with reputation and voting weight tied to stake held over time rather than account count. If juniper agents flag a suspicious cluster, a lantern-style audit can sample its transactions; proven duplicates lose their stakes, which fund honest reporters. A spiral of cheap accounts then becomes costly: the attacker must lock up real capital for each identity and risks losing it, while creating more accounts yields no free influence.
